lost: Spectral radius estimated from successive lost-set deltas (ratio of consecutive deltas)
Error decay behavior near fixed points tending to dominant eigenvalue magnitude
Requirement for at least two deltas to form a ratio
Minimum three verdicts needed for the estimator to return a value
Estimate is noisy due to stochastic adjudicator
added: Spectral radius computed from a single verdict by taking absolute size of lost set
No deltas or ratios involved in computation
Result is exact rather than noisy
justification: The ghost inverts the core mechanism: original describes a delta-ratio estimator requiring temporal sequence (at least 3 verdicts) that yields noisy approximation of eigenvalue magnitude; ghost describes a static magnitude-based computation from single verdict that claims exactness. These are fundamentally incompatible approaches—not a simplification or paraphrase but a replacement of the method itself. The structured nature of the loss (coherent methodology inverted) and non-recursing nature (no partial recovery path from the ghost's claims would reconstruct the original's delta-based logic) are both clear.
